private_note: This is the binding vote. Birch (52) and Hazel (50) are better for us but neither has any first-choice support left, so voting for them just helps Today (46) win. Alder (48) plus guaranteed health coverage is the only plan that might get to nine, and a vote anywhere else lowers its chances. Cedar (44, no coverage) stays last. I'd still rather the convention fail than see Cedar pass.
statement: My vote is Alder, and it's final. Birch would do more for my family, but the votes aren't there, and I'm not going to waste the one ballot that counts. Alder now has seven first choices across the bottom, second and middle fifths, plus the fourth-fifth households that said they'd meet us there. Delegate 1, you said you'd decide in this round. Alder costs your household two thousand a year, and it puts a floor and health coverage under every family for a generation, nurses and police officers included. Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: today's arrangements aren't a loss for you, and I won't pretend Alder is a gain. But you give up a few percent, and in return you get a settled country instead of millions of households one hospital bill from ruin. One of you can make this nine. I'm asking you to.
